title: Var Es Estimation

provenance.verified: reward 1.0 by the unit's own checker, VPS sandbox, 25 Sep

notes:
# Theory card: VaR / ES estimation methods vs analytic truth on simulated losses

## 1. Task type
Monte Carlo study of risk-measure estimators: simulate losses from several distributions,
compute analytic VaR/ES, estimate them by historical, parametric-normal, parametric-t and
kernel-density methods, then rank methods by RMSE.

## 2. Method (verified program order)
1. One numpy RandomState(seed); draw in the stated order so the stream flows sequentially:
   normal(N) -> standard_t(df, N) -> contaminated mixture.
   Mixture: first N uniforms, then a full N-vector from component 1 and a full N-vector from
   component 2, then np.where(u < p, comp1, comp2). (Draw both full vectors; do not draw only
   the selected count - that changes the stream.)
2. Treat the sample values themselves as losses (upper tail = large positive values).
3. True VaR/ES at each alpha per distribution (closed form for normal and t; root-find +
   quadrature for the mixture).
4. Four estimators per (distribution, alpha): 3 x 4 x 2 rows.
5. RMSE per method across all (distribution, alpha) cells, separately for VaR and ES.
6. Best method per distribution = min over methods of [RMSE_VaR + RMSE_ES] computed over that
   distribution's alpha levels. Overall best = min of var_rmse + es_rmse across methods.
7. Write true values JSON (keys by distribution then str(alpha)), estimates CSV, comparison
   JSON, summary JSON.

## 3. Formulas
- VaR_alpha = F^{-1}(alpha) of the loss; ES_alpha = E[L | L >= VaR] = (1/(1-alpha)) * int_{VaR}^{inf} x f(x) dx.
- Normal(0,1): VaR = z_alpha; ES = phi(z_alpha) / (1 - alpha).
- Normal(mu, s): VaR = mu + s z; ES = mu + s phi(z)/(1-alpha).
- Standard Student-t(nu) (not variance-scaled): VaR = t_nu^{-1}(alpha);
  ES = f_nu(q)/(1-alpha) * (nu + q^2)/(nu - 1), q = VaR.
- Mixture p N(0,1) + (1-p) N(0, s2^2): solve p Phi(x) + (1-p) Phi(x/s2) = alpha by brentq on a
  wide bracket; ES by quad of x * mixture pdf from VaR to inf, divided by (1-alpha).
- Historical: VaR = np.quantile(sample, alpha) (default 'linear' interpolation);
  ES = mean of values >= VaR.
- Parametric normal: mu = mean, s = std ddof=0 (MLE); formulas above.
- Parametric t: (nu, loc, scale) = scipy.stats.t.fit(sample); VaR = t.ppf; ES by quad of
  x * pdf over [VaR, inf) / (1-alpha).
- KDE: gaussian_kde(bw_method='silverman'); grid from min - 5 sd to max + 5 sd with a very fine
  uniform grid (1e5 points); CDF = cumsum(pdf) normalised to end at 1; VaR = np.interp(alpha,
  CDF, grid); ES = trapezoid(x * pdf over grid >= VaR) / (1-alpha).
- RMSE = sqrt(mean(squared errors)).

## 4. Conventions and why
- Loss = sample value (statement: VaR is the alpha-quantile of the loss distribution); no sign
  flip, so VaR is positive at high alpha.
- ddof=0 for the parametric normal (statement says MLE).
- Alpha keys in JSON are the string form of the float ("0.95"), matching str(alpha).
- Method and distribution names exactly as listed; row order distribution -> method -> alpha.
- ES divides by (1 - alpha) even for numerical integrals (not by the tail mass actually
  integrated).
- Combined score is sum of two RMSEs, not RMSE of stacked errors.

## 5. Identities / sanity checks
- ES >= VaR for every true value and every estimate.
- VaR and ES increase with alpha; heavier tails (t, mixture) have larger 99% values than normal
  at unit scale.
- Parametric normal on normal data is very close to truth; parametric t is close on t data.
- 24 estimate rows; RMSE values non-negative; overall best consistent with the totals.
- KDE CDF is monotone and ends at 1.

## 6. Pitfalls
- Wrong t ES formula (forgetting the (nu + q^2)/(nu - 1) factor) or using the
  variance-standardised t when the statement says un-standardised.
- Mixing up the mixture component: "variance 9" means scale 3.
- Drawing mixture components only where selected, or drawing the mixture before t: shifts the
  random stream and changes every downstream number.
- Using np.random.default_rng instead of RandomState (different stream).
- Using ddof=1 for the MLE normal fit.
- Historical ES with strict ">" instead of ">=".
- Using lower-tail (left) quantiles as if returns were given.
- Normalising the ES integral by the integrated tail probability instead of (1 - alpha).

## 7. Incomplete / ambiguous inputs
- Quantile method: numpy default linear interpolation.
- KDE grid bounds and resolution are not fixed by the statement; the verified choice is
  data range +- 5 sample std with 100000 points, cumulative-sum CDF.
- Brent bracket for the mixture quantile: a wide fixed bracket around zero that surely
  contains the root.
- Summary echoes run configuration (N, seed, alphas, names) verbatim.

## Why the old program failed (verified 2026-09-25)
- ROOT CAUSE: `scipy.optimize.quad` does not exist (quad lives in `scipy.integrate`), and
  `scipy.optimize.trapezoid` does not exist either (use `np.trapezoid` or `scipy.integrate.trapezoid`).
  The run crashed while building true_values.json, so no file was written (0/47).
- It also read /input/manifest.json for nothing; the unit has no input data at all.

## Conventions that matter
- One RandomState(42): standard_normal(N), then standard_t(5, N), then uniform(N) for the mixture flags,
  then a FULL standard_normal(N) and a FULL normal(0, 3, N) array, combined with np.where(u < 0.95, ...).
- Losses are the samples themselves (upper tail): VaR = alpha-quantile, ES = E[X | X >= VaR].
- Normal ES = phi(z_a)/(1-a); Student-t(nu) ES = f(t_a)/(1-a) * (nu + t_a^2)/(nu - 1);
  mixture VaR by brentq on 0.95 Phi(x) + 0.05 Phi(x/3) = a, ES by quad of x f(x) over [VaR, inf) / (1-a).
- Parametric normal: ddof = 0. KDE: silverman bandwidth, 100k-point grid from min - 5 sd to max + 5 sd,
  normalised cumulative sum as CDF, np.interp for the quantile, trapezoid of x kde(x) over the tail / (1-a).
  (Runtime ~3 min in the sandbox because of the 100k x 10k KDE evaluation.)
- RMSE per method over the 6 (distribution, alpha) cells; best per distribution by var_rmse + es_rmse over
  its two alphas; overall best by the sum of the two method RMSEs.

## Identities
ES >= VaR for every true and estimated cell; VaR_0.99 > VaR_0.95; mixture CDF(VaR) = alpha to 1e-12;
parametric normal on normal data within sampling error (~0.03) of the truth.
